attempted_claim: Fix a translation-invariant Hormander nondegenerate phase phi on B(0,1)x[-1,1]x(R^3\{0}) satisfying Bourgain's condition with strict positivity at the origin, Omega(1)-coniness and Omega(1)-twistiness in the sense of Nadjimzadah, and finite contact order at most 4, hence admitting no Kakeya compression surface (e.g. an SL2-type phase known to satisfy these stable conditions). Call a compact set E subset R^3 a twisty-phase Kakeya set for this phi if for every direction xi/|xi| in S^2 it contains a unit-length phi-curve arc in that direction with basepoint in B(0,1). Prove or disprove that every such E satisfies dim_H(E)>=49/20. A complete answer is either a rigorous proof of dim_H(E)>=49/20 for all such E (by polynomial partitioning for variable-coefficient tubes combined with Wolff-hairbrush plus coniness/twistiness incidence bounds) or an explicit compact E0 for this fixed phi containing one curve in every direction with dim_H(E0)<49/20, with verification of containment and dimension.
decisive_failure: The investigation concretely attempted both horns of the prove-or-disprove target (hairbrush plus partitioning proof; compression-based disproof) and a quantitative recovery test, but the exact Nadjimzadah coney-twisty wall estimate with constants could not be reconstructed locally, and no alternative compression mechanism compatible with the hypotheses was found. No independently valuable original increment emerged; only routine numerology was produced.
